description:
FILED s396 while finishing #314 family F-C (n-at-a-time foreach, task #329).

PCL has read-only ARRAYS (fixed-size storage, %p-array-readonly-p) but no
read-only SCALARS, so perl's

    Modification of a read-only value attempted

never fires for a scalar.  Probed vs perl 5.40.3:

    my $r = \undef; $$r = 5;      perl DIES        PCL writes silently
    for (1,2,3) { $_ = 9 }        perl DIES        PCL writes silently

MEASURED POPULATION so far: SIX rows of t/op/for-many.t — every remaining
failure in that file except the two "invalid perl must be rejected" rows
(CLAUDE.md principle 9, out of scope):

    aliased rvalue / aliased rvalue threw the correct exception
    for () () aliases 3 / for () () aliases 4
    padded with literal undef / padded with literal undef threw the correct
      exception / side effects observed

They all come from ONE perl fact: a literal `undef` (or any literal) in a
foreach list is READ-ONLY, so assigning to a loop variable aliased to it dies,
and the file checks BOTH the exception and that the array was left alone.  The
same fact is what perl pads a short final chunk with, which is why #329's
rewrite pads with writable slots instead and diverges here.

THE COST TO WEIGH BEFORE BUILDING (this is why it is not done): the check
belongs in `box-set`, which is THE hot path of every assignment in every
generated program.  CLAUDE.md's standing instruction is to flag any bugfix that
slows execution, and Target A is "beat perl".  So the design question is not
"can we" but "where does the flag live so the check is free when it is off" —
e.g. a distinct BOX TYPE for read-only scalars (dispatch, not a branch), the
way read-only arrays are a distinct STORAGE (no fill pointer) rather than a
per-array flag consulted on push.  That precedent is in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp
near %p-array-readonly-p and its fable-answers-s318 §2 note.

BEFORE BUILDING: measure the wider population.  Six rows in one companion file
is not enough on its own; grep the fail baseline and the companion snapshot for
"read-only" first.
subject: No read-only SCALARS: `Modification of a read-only value attempted` never fires (6 rows of op/for-many.t)
